newsitem.title: UK: Healthy demand boosts Med crude, W.Af sees upturn.
newsitem.headline: Healthy demand boosts Med crude, W.Af sees upturn.

text.p: Refinery demand boosted regional crude prices in the Mediterranean with Iraqi oil not expected to relieve market tightness before July, traders said.
Urals' ascent continued, with a deal reported done on Tuesday at Dated Brent -$1.10, seven cents up on a trade on Monday.
"Refiners want to buy, they are looking at very good margins and an outright price that is quite low...also they want to store oil to take advantage of the contango," said one trader.
Most of the first and second decade Urals programme was now committed, dealers said.
Many traders were not expecting first liftings of Iraqi Kirkuk under the second term of the United Nations oil-for-food agreement to start until July.
And most of the early cargoes would go straight to refiners systems, they said.
"People have homes for all the first cargoes...we won't see anything being offered spot," a trader said.
Other sour grades were not seen on offer in the Med, with Iranian grades sold out for June.
A narrow Brent/Dubai spread was offering a glimmer of hope to the beleaguered West African market, creating buying interest from Far East refiners.
A July loading cargo each of Nigerian Qua Iboe and Equatorial Guinean Zafiro were sold into South Korea by a major.
"There is demand from the South Korean and Japanese for various of the lighter grades for August arrival," a trader said.
Meanwhile, trading houses still holding June barrels were looking for buyers in the U.S. Gulf.
Some Qua Iboe barrels were heard sold earlier in the week to a U.S. refiner at a weak Dated Brent +23 cents.
